subject: QBR prep: capacity playbook readout & OKR asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR prep: capacity playbook readout & OKR asks

Team—

Ahead of next week’s QBR I wanted to surface the draft capacity playbook and the concrete OKR asks we should take to the exec table. This thread contains the working readout and two attached artifacts (capacity_model_v2.xlsx, batching-sim-results.csv). High level:

- Runway: with current commitments and typical batching patterns we have ~11–13 weeks of comfortable headroom on our Dedicated pools before hitting 85% utilization on the primary GPU tier.
- Shortfall scenarios: two demand surge scenarios in the model (S1: regional marketing ramp, S2: partner pilot surge) push us to 95% within 4–6 weeks absent mitigations.
- Unit economics: per-token cost currently dominated by idle time + small-batch overheads; batching and KV caching reduce unit cost by ~18–28% in our sims, but introduce 40–120ms median tail depending on traffic shape.

Proposed QBR asks (please review and flag):
1) Approve the 2-month burst budget (reserve + spot tranche) to cover S1 & S2: ask = $220k/mo for May–June.
2) Prioritize two infra OKRs for Q2: (A) rollout KV prefix caching to 80% of high-frequency routes; (B) fast-fail routing to low-cost model variants under heavy load.
3) Greenlight the batching experiment (1-week canary) with the 2% latency SLO exception for real-user routes.

Action items for owners:
- Jonas: validate the projected latency tail (from batching-sim-results.csv) and flag any routes where latency uptick > 120ms by 2028-03-21 EOD.
- Rishi: confirm whether finance can retroactively reassign $150k from unallocated reserve to the burst tranche.
- Marissa: produce a one-page exec summary (slide) we can use in the QBR deck — due 03/20 COB.

I’ve kept the spreadsheet model conservative on demand growth; happy to walk through numbers on a quick call.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Infrastructure Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs):
- capacity_model_v2.xlsx (Excel, 1.2MB, 7 tabs)
- batching-sim-results.csv (CSV, 320KB)

Subject: Re: QBR prep: capacity playbook readout & OKR asks

Thanks Hannah — this is excellent work and very crisp. Two quick requests before I sign off to Exec:

1) Please produce a one-paragraph executive summary (bullet + single graph) that calls out the single biggest risk and the single biggest cost lever. I want this on slide 2.
2) Mark the asks with prioritization (Must/Should/Nice-to-have). We should only take the Must-level items to the QBR ask stage.

Jonas/Rishi: loop in if you see any fatal flaws in the assumptions. Hannah — can you get the summary + prioritized list by COB tomorrow (03/20)?

-LB

Adding a quick finance perspective — high level:
- The burst tranche ask ($220k/mo) looks directionally reasonable if we want immediate coverage for S1/S2. Finance can cover $70k from existing marketplace credits and ~$80k from reallocated reserved funds; the remaining ~$70k would require a short approval (paperwork takes ~3 business days).
- Important signal: rolling caching/batching reduces incremental spend but increases forecasting variance. If we commit to the caching OKR, we should also ask Product to freeze major model changes on high-frequency routes for the quarter (to avoid repeated cache invalidations).

I’ll follow up with a short note to Finance ops with the numbers.

-Rishi

Team — thanks for the quick turn. Attached is the brief exec summary (qbr-exec-summary-1p.pdf) and the final runbook linked in Drive. Quick note on timing and the canaries:

- Canaries: We’ll run the batching canary starting 2028-03-25 for 5 business days on 3 low-latency-safe routes. Operational rollbacks are scripted; if median latency > +120ms for any route we abort and auto-roll to current config.
- KV caching rollout: phase 1 to 80% of high-frequency routes scheduled 2028-04-02–2028-04-09; we’ll gate by 99th percentile tail on small-batch routes.
- Exec ask packaging: Must = burst tranche approval (220k/mo), KV caching OKR, canary approval with the 2% latency SLO exception. Should = expanded spot tranche for multi-region redundancy.

Related links: https://drive.redwood/company/qbr/2028/capacity_playbook_v2

I’ll be available for a run-through tomorrow morning.
